::: {.playbook-summary}
### How to use this page

Find the task, copy the structure—not necessarily the exact variable names—and read the code aloud before running it. Replace placeholders with fields from the data dictionary and inspect the result.
:::

## Start an analysis

| Task | Code | Read it as |
|---|---|---|
| Load core packages | `library(tidyverse)` | Make tidyverse functions available |
| Load model helpers | `library(broom)` | Make tidy model summaries available |
| Import a CSV | `patients <- read_csv("data/patients.csv")` | Read this file and store it as `patients` |
| Inspect structure | `glimpse(patients)` | Show variables, types and example values |
| View first rows | `head(patients)` | Show the first six observations |
| Count observations | `nrow(patients)` | Return the number of rows |
| List variable names | `names(patients)` | Return the column names |

```r
#| eval: false

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

patients <- read_csv("data/patients.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(patients)
```

## Prepare data

| Question | Function | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Which variables? | `select()` | `select(patient_id, age, treatment, outcome)` |
| Which observations? | `filter()` | `filter(age >= 18, !is.na(outcome))` |
| Which new variables? | `mutate()` | `mutate(age_decade = age / 10)` |
| Which order? | `arrange()` | `arrange(desc(outcome))` |
| Which names? | `rename()` | `rename(age_years = age)` |
| Which unique records? | `distinct()` | `distinct(patient_id, .keep_all = TRUE)` |

```r
#| eval: false

analysis_data <- patients |>
  select(patient_id, age, treatment, outcome) |>
  filter(age >= 18, !is.na(outcome)) |>
  mutate(
    age_decade = age / 10,
    older_adult = age >= 65
  )
```

## Summarise data

| Task | Example |
|---|---|
| Number of observations | `summarise(patients = n())` |
| Mean | `mean(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Median | `median(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Standard deviation | `sd(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Interquartile range | `IQR(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Minimum and maximum | `range(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |
| Count categories | `count(treatment)` |
| Summarise within groups | `group_by(treatment) |> summarise(...)` |

```r
#| eval: false

analysis_data |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    patients = n(),
    mean_outcome = mean(outcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_outcome = sd(outcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_outcome = median(outcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_outcome = IQR(outcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Handle missing values

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Is a value missing? | `is.na(outcome)` |
| Is a value recorded? | `!is.na(outcome)` |
| Count missing values | `sum(is.na(outcome))` |
| Keep recorded outcomes | `filter(!is.na(outcome))` |
| Ignore missing values in a summary | `mean(outcome, na.rm = TRUE)` |

Never use `outcome == NA`; it cannot answer the question. Missingness should be counted and justified, not made invisible.

## Create figures

```r
#| eval: false

# Histogram
analysis_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = outcome)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Outcome (units)", y = "Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

# Group comparison
analysis_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = outcome)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Outcome (units)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Relationship
analysis_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = exposure, y = outcome)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Run common analyses

| Clinical question | Function structure |
|---|---|
| Compare two independent means | `t.test(outcome ~ group, data = analysis_data)` |
| Compare paired measurements | `t.test(after, before, paired = TRUE)` |
| Compare more than two means | `aov(outcome ~ group, data = analysis_data)` |
| Compare categorical variables | `chisq.test(table(exposure, outcome))` |
| Estimate correlation | `cor.test(x, y, method = "pearson")` |
| Fit linear regression | `lm(outcome ~ exposure + age, data = analysis_data)` |
| Fit logistic regression | `glm(event ~ exposure + age, data = analysis_data, family = binomial())` |

## Work with results

```r
#| eval: false

model <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + age, data = analysis_data)

summary(model)
coef(model)
confint(model)
fitted(model)
residuals(model)

model_table <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE)
```

## Predict and evaluate

```r
#| eval: false

test_predictions <- test_data |>
  mutate(
    predicted_risk = predict(model, newdata = test_data, type = "response"),
    predicted_positive = predicted_risk >= 0.20
  )

test_predictions |>
  count(predicted_positive, observed_outcome)
```

## Export and preserve

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Export a table | `write_csv(results, "results.csv")` |
| Save an R object | `saveRDS(model, "model.rds")` |
| Reopen an R object | `readRDS("model.rds")` |
| Record software versions | `sessionInfo()` |
| Make randomness reproducible | `set.seed(2026)` immediately before the random step |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Before trusting the output

Check the number of rows, variable types, reference groups, outcome coding, missing observations, units, assumptions, and whether the result answers the original clinical question.
:::
